findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: bellman_start, bellman_confirm, bellman_send, bellman_surface, bellman_audit, bellman_report · Private data: bellman_connect, bellman_confirm, bellman_invite, bellman_send, bellman_public_name, bellman_decide, bellman_fs, bellman_memory · Public sink: bellman_start, bellman_confirm, bellman_send, bellman_surface, bellman_decide, bellman_fs, bellman_memory · Destructive: bellman_confirm, bellman_send, bellman_evict, bellman_fs.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: bellman_start, bellman_confirm, bellman_send, bellman_surface, bellman_audit, bellman_report · Private data: bellman_connect, bellman_confirm, bellman_invite, bellman_send, bellman_public_name, bellman_decide, bellman_fs, bellman_memory · Public sink: bellman_start, bellman_confirm, bellman_send, bellman_surface, bellman_decide, bellman_fs, bellman_memory · Destructive: bellman_confirm, bellman_send, bellman_evict, bellman_fs

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
